explanation: In Turkey, cheek kissing is a common greeting among friends and acquaintances of the same gender, typically one kiss on each cheek. However, between men and women in more conservative or formal settings, a handshake or nod is preferred. It is less common among strangers or in very formal business contexts.
local_tip: When in doubt, wait for the other person to initiate the cheek kiss, and mirror their gesture.
regional_note: In more conservative or religious circles, especially in rural areas, opposite-gender cheek kissing may be avoided; among younger, urban populations it is more accepted.

also_check.note: Cheek kissing is not customary; bowing is the standard greeting.
Cheek kissing (la bise) is common, but the number of kisses varies by region.
Cheek kissing between men is common, but between unrelated men and women it is generally avoided.
